items.summary:
Carlos Ferrando, the engineer behind Closca foldable bike helmets, said his company was overjoyed after New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani appeared wearing one while promoting cycling in the city.

Mamdani had earlier drawn social media criticism for riding without a helmet before posting videos joking with influencer Carson and Councilman Lincoln Restler as they put on and removed Closca helmets, which originate from Sumacàrcer, a town of 1,000 people about 6,000 kilometers (3,720 miles) from New York.

Ferrando said he sent the mayor an X message congratulating him for supporting biking while also criticizing his lack of helmet use and mentioning his product. He could not say whether a team member saw it or whether the design's one-second folding mechanism caught attention at MoMA's gift store, where Closca is sold.

The helmets come in two models priced between €80 and €130 and are available in New York and San Francisco stores as well as the United Kingdom, Japan, Germany, Spain, and online. The brand was previously covered by media after Google executives bought and recommended it in 2017.

Ferrando's Closca company has grown to 15 employees, produces its helmets in China, and still needs higher volume before expanding further.
items.title: Spanish Foldable Helmet Maker Celebrates Endorsement from New York Mayor Mamdani

items.summary:
The U.S. Senate passed a bill to speed up permitting for energy infrastructure on Nov. 19, with environmental groups warning it would also accelerate fossil fuel development by weakening existing protections.

On a 62-33 vote, the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) drew support from pro-environment Democratic senators including Rhode Island's Sheldon Whitehouse, who co-sponsored the legislation.

The bill would ease permitting for renewable energy and transmission lines while shortening review timelines under laws such as the Clean Water Act, Endangered Species Act, and National Environmental Policy Act. Fewer projects would require full environmental review, assessment periods would shrink, and the window to sue over approved projects would narrow.

Environmental organizations argue the technology-neutral fast track applies equally to fossil fuels and data centers. Brad Campbell of the Conservation Law Foundation called it a 'one-way ratchet for fossil fuels' given an administration he said is hostile to clean energy.

Above ground, BAAJA could lower barriers for oil, gas, and mining projects on public and tribal lands, drawing condemnation from several Native American organizations. At sea, Oceana warned the bill would roll back ocean protections and open the door to more offshore drilling.

Section 1401 of the bill bars agencies from revising permits once granted, even if they are expedited or later found legally flawed. Oceana said such approvals would become nearly impossible to revisit.

Whitehouse claimed BAAJA lowers emissions by 1.5 gigatons through 2040, though that figure is a projection rather than an established outcome.

In an open letter, more than 120 scientists urged the House of Representatives to reject the bill as it prepares to vote next week.
items.title: Senate clean-energy permitting bill could fast-track fossil fuels

items.summary:
Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) leaders staged a biryani protest at Hyderabad's Bavarchi restaurant on November 26, targeting Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over the alleged failure to deliver two lakh jobs promised by the Congress-led Telangana government. BRS leaders Manne Krishank, Putta Vishnuvardhan Reddy and Mutha Jai Simha carried a portrait of Rahul Gandhi while eating biryani inside the restaurant as their symbolic protest.

The demonstration turned confrontational when Congress workers arrived at the venue, leading to heated arguments that escalated into a physical clash in which plates were allegedly thrown between the two groups. Police intervened and restored order before the confrontation could worsen. Congress Rajya Sabha MP Anil Kumar Yadav criticized the BRS leaders for choosing this form of protest.

The biryani protest followed another clash on November 19 at a pension distribution program in Hyderabad's LB Nagar constituency, which erupted over access to the stage during an official government event. BRS MLA D Sudheer Reddy objected to Congress leaders including former MP Madhu Yaskhi Goud and several corporators occupying the dais while around 200 BRS workers reportedly waited outside for nearly two hours.

During that earlier confrontation, arguments escalated into slogan-shouting and physical altercations as workers from both parties pushed one another. Police removed Sudheer Reddy and other BRS workers from the stage, prompting the MLA to accuse police of favoring Congress. He later staged a sit-in and threatened to file a formal complaint with the Director General of Police against the officials involved.
items.title: BRS and Congress Workers Clash Over Biryani Protest Targeting Rahul Gandhi

items.summary:
Russian President Vladimir Putin signed a decree on Thursday approving his country's development strategy for the Arctic region through 2035. The decree, titled 'Strategy for the Development of the Russian Arctic Zone and the Provision of National Security in the Arctic,' was published alongside the 59-page strategy document, which includes an annex.

The decree directs the government to develop a comprehensive plan covering Russia's Arctic Zone and the Transarctic Transport Corridor within six months. The completed plan is to be submitted to the Presidential Council for Strategic Development and National Projects for consideration.

According to the decree, it enters into force on the day of its publication. The strategy document states that implementation will occur in stages: a first stage from 2026 to 2030, followed by a second stage from 2031 to 2035. Subsequent stages are set to take place every six years.

The document provides for adjustments after each completed stage or at the discretion of the Russian president.
items.title: Putin Approves Russia's Arctic Development Strategy Through 2035

items.summary:
Nahid Islam, convener of Bangladesh's National Citizen Party (NCP), demanded the removal and apology of West Bengal Transport Minister Arjun Singh over remarks threatening to "take over" Dhaka. The exchange could intensify strained India-Bangladesh ties amid tensions over Sheikh Hasina's extradition.

Islam said on X that Singh directly challenged Bangladesh's sovereignty by threatening to occupy the country, calling the statement an affront to 180 million people and their independence won through sacrifice. He demanded Singh be removed from the cabinet and offer an unconditional apology.

The remarks come as India-Bangladesh relations remain sensitive following Hasina's fall in August 2024. She fled to India after a student-led uprising, remains there since then, while Bangladesh has sought her extradition.

Singh made his statement linking Bangladesh's internal violence against Hindus to a possible Indian response. He said by December 16 they would take over Bangladesh and avenge killings of Hindus in the country.

December 16 carries significance as Victory Day, marking Bangladesh's victory in the 1971 Liberation War.

Islam criticized both New Delhi for its silence after more than 48 hours without action against Singh, and Dhaka for failing to respond strongly enough. He also accused India of sheltering a "murderer" and allowing its territory to be used against Bangladesh.

Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal sentenced Hasina to death in absentia over crimes linked to the crackdown on protesters. Her spokesperson Syed Mozammel Ali said she wants to travel from Delhi to Dhaka on Biman Bangladesh Airlines, but that demand was rejected by tribunal chief prosecutor Md Aminul Islam.

With Hasina's proposed return looming over December 16, Nahid's remarks could add friction between Dhaka and New Delhi.
items.title: Bangladeshi Opposition Leader Demands Removal of Indian Minister Over 'Take Over' Threat

items.summary:
Russian President Vladimir Putin called Thursday for the broad adoption of artificial intelligence across Russia's economy and society, proposing an update to the country's national AI strategy.

Speaking at a conference in Moscow, Putin said he wanted AI use to expand into all sectors and aspects of daily life. He argued that simply having advanced AI no longer guarantees technological leadership or long-term development.

Putin proposed updating the existing national AI strategy through 2036 and approving an action plan for AI development. He described AI as reaching a new level of autonomy, moving from digital applications into physical-world use with capabilities expected to keep growing.

He said such changes could become revolutionary in many industries over time. Putin framed AI as an opportunity to address Russia's demographic challenges and labor shortages by strengthening the country's potential.

Putin noted that costs for advanced foundational models are rising and pointed to electricity, power grid capacity, and component shortages as bottlenecks requiring colossal investment. He said Russia is betting on sovereign foundational models and will keep developing them.

He warned against dependence on foreign systems, saying Russia must avoid situations where technology can be shut down remotely or covertly used to serve other interests. Putin stressed that the country must never allow AI innovations to be turned against its interests.
items.title: Putin Calls for Widespread AI Use and Strategy Update

items.summary:
Kim Jong Un inspected two nuclear materials production factories, one newly inaugurated and another being expanded, calling for the development of more nuclear weapons days after declining President Donald Trump's offer to meet during his recent Asian trip. The inspections were reported Thursday by North Korea's Korean Central News Agency.

KCNA photos showed Kim touring facilities with dense rows believed to be centrifuges used to produce weapons-grade uranium, as well as halls displaying what appeared to be warheads. Some images were blurred. On Wednesday he also visited a nuclear-powered equipment production base and a nuclear research institute.

Kim framed the visits around strengthening North Korea's defense against 'variable nuclear threats approaching the Korean Peninsula moment by moment,' according to KCNA. He called his possession of nuclear weapons an 'irreversible reality' and said deploying low-yield battlefield nuclear weapons was crucial given its border with South Korea, which he described as the most dangerous enemy state.

Moon Seong Mook, an analyst for the Seoul-based Korea Research Institute for National Strategy, said Kim wanted to display his evolving arsenal and reject future denuclearization talks. Moon added that the visit likely checked on progress toward nuclear goals ahead of a year-end Workers' Party conference.

South Korea's Defense Ministry took Kim's comments on battlefield weapons seriously and reaffirmed its military readiness under an alliance with the U.S. The Joint Chiefs of Staff declined to analyze KCNA's report, citing confidentiality for South Korea and the United States.

Trump reiterated his desire to restore diplomacy after visiting China last week for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, but no meeting occurred because Pyongyang did not publicly respond to his overture. In an interview with the New York Post this week, Trump dismissed claims that Kim rebuffed him, saying a meeting had simply 'not really been the right time.'

Trump said he could revive diplomacy at any time by restarting letter exchanges from his first term, though he acknowledged the two leaders had not corresponded recently. Kim has previously indicated he would return to talks if the U.S. drops its 'hostile policy' and respects North Korea's status as a nuclear state.

Rafael Grossi, director general of the International Atomic Energy Agency, last week assessed that North Korea was expanding its original uranium enrichment facility at Yongbyon, calling it 'a cause for serious concern.' South Korea's Unification Minister Chung Dong-young said last year that North Korea operated four uranium enrichment facilities running every day.

North Korea has disclosed a few uranium enrichment sites since showing one to visiting American scholars in 2010. It did not say where the factories Kim visited this week are located, though outside experts assessed an earlier June disclosure was likely another facility at Yongbyon.
items.title: North Korean leader vows to expand nuclear arsenal after rejecting Trump meeting

Sakana AI has released Sakana Namazu Small, a 30-billion-parameter reasoning model built on NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Nano base and trained in-house. The lab reports that it scores higher than the larger 120B Nemotron 3 Super across its average of 25 benchmarks.

The model is labeled 30B-A3B, meaning 3 billion parameters are active out of a total of 30 billion. Sakana says it targets everyday conversation, web-search research, and long-document reading, organizing information before reasoning step by step toward an answer.

Sakana started from the pretrained Nemotron 3 Nano base rather than NVIDIA's post-trained release, then applied continued pretraining and post-training on top of methods used for its larger Namazu model. The underlying architecture is a hybrid Mamba-Transformer mixture-of-experts design with up to 1 million-token context.

On self-reported benchmarks, the model averages 60.1 across 25 tests, ahead of Nemotron 3 Super's 56.2 and Nano's 50.2. Its strongest result is BrowseComp at 73.5, roughly twice Super's 36.1.

The model also leads on several long-document tasks: DeepSearchQA reaches 84.3 versus 65.4 for Super, LLM-jp LongBench hits 86.0 versus 67.0 for Nano, FaithEval scores 78.3 versus 59.1 for Super, and citation-focused ALCE lands at 60.2.

Closed-book knowledge remains its weak area: SimpleQA Verified falls to 6.8, below Super's 18.1 and Nano's 9.1, while HealthBench drops to 40.6 versus Nano's 47.5. Sakana notes that tasks relying only on internal knowledge did not improve much.

Across the full suite, Namazu Small beats Nemotron 3 Super on 13 of 25 benchmarks and outperforms Nemotron 3 Nano on 22 of 25.
items.title: Sakana AI Launches 30B Reasoning Model Named Namazu Small

items.summary:
An International Court of Justice ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in 2017 places China in a diplomatic bind between defending its strategic partner and upholding international justice.

China has substantial economic interests tied to Myanmar, including oil and gas pipelines connecting Rakhine state's coast to Beijing. The court ordered Myanmar to cease violations against the Rohingya, prevent future ones, prosecute those responsible, allow displaced Rohingya to return, and reunite families.

In a statement released on November 19, the same day as the judgment, the UN Refugee Agency reported more than 1.3 million Rohingya refugees remain displaced, most in Bangladesh while over 200,000 are internally displaced within Rakhine state.

China acknowledged international judicial institutions but said the court acted beyond its jurisdiction and flagged 'overreach in interpretation,' a stance consistent with its non-interference foreign policy principle. However, because China is party to the 1948 Genocide Convention, the ruling complicates Beijing's ability to justify restraint over Myanmar solely on sovereignty grounds.

China could pressure Myanmar's military leadership to investigate the crimes against the Rohingya, but such moves would likely strain cooperation on border security and investment. The Gambia filed its complaint in 2019 and can seek UN Security Council action if Myanmar fails to comply.
items.title: China Faces Diplomatic Dilemma After ICJ Genocide Ruling Against Myanmar

items.summary:
Severe storms are disrupting Thanksgiving travel across the nation, with New York City rescheduling its centennial Macy's Day Parade to Saturday because wind gusts could reach up to 60 mph.

Forecasters say an East Coast storm is the primary concern as it becomes better organized and brings strong winds and heavy rain that could cause coastal flooding. The system should move on, mostly wrapping up by Saturday.

The Trump administration has proposed new tariffs targeting goods from 14 major U.S. trading partners, including China, Japan and the European Union. Proposed rates may reach 40% on Chinese imports, 35% on Vietnamese goods, and 20-25% on products from other targeted nations.

The White House lists a separate 'deal' rate for each country that would apply if trade talks progress positively; China's deal rate is set at 20%, below its proposed rate of 40%. The new tariffs fall under Section 301, which the administration says targets countries with structural excess capacity in manufactured goods.

Federal scientists are testing air, soil and water in Eastern Iowa for lead contamination after the U.S. Army detonated thousands of pounds of unstable lead azide at the Middletown ammunition plant to safely dispose of a bomb-making compound.
items.title: Storms disrupt Thanksgiving travel; judge blocks Trump over ABC license

items.summary:
The French government plans to triple the volume of its upcoming technology-neutral renewable energy auction from an initially proposed 500 MW to 1.5 GW, according to a Nov. 25 announcement during a press briefing.

The increase follows concerns raised by industry associations that had called for the mechanism to be open to all renewable energy technologies rather than favoring specific ones.

The government submitted draft tender rules with the original 500 MW figure before raising it; the auction is expected to launch in the coming days.

A second major change introduces a single baseload reference price, known as M0 baseload, for all technologies instead of calculating each technology's reference price according to its own generation profile.

Under the new approach, the calculation will use the national monthly average of wholesale spot electricity prices across all hours of the day rather than reflecting individual generation patterns such as solar's midday bell-shaped curve.

The change would expose renewable energy producers more directly to fluctuations in wholesale electricity prices and reduce the influence of their generation profiles on reference-price calculations.
items.title: France Triples Planned Renewable Energy Auction Volume to 1.5 GW

items.summary:
Nyana rooiwalensis, a nearly complete skull of a large-bodied but juvenile dinosaur from the Late Triassic Elliot Formation in southern Africa, provides evidence that rapid growth characteristic of later giant sauropods was already emerging among their ancestors.

The fossil is notable as the first exceptionally well-preserved Late Triassic dinosaur skull recovered, including structures such as the braincase, palate, and bones associated with the tongue, throat, and eye. This preservation lets researchers study how skull proportions change with age in ways that fragmentary material cannot.

Despite an estimated body mass of roughly 400 kilogrammes, osteohistology—the microscopic examination of bone tissue—indicates Nyana was still very young when it died, preserving at most two lines of seasonal growth. This combination of substantial size and early life stage supports the idea that rapid growth was already important in early sauropodomorph evolution.

The discovery also highlights South Africa's fossil record as central to reconstructing dinosaur evolution. Before this find, the lower Triassic portion of the Elliot Formation had yielded only fragmentary skull material from another species called Kholumolumo; earlier well-preserved specimens came from younger rocks.

Across corporate America, leaders who lied about relationships with subordinates have typically been removed from their positions. Jensen Huang's return to the helm of Nvidia suggests that this pattern may now carry an exception.

The temporarily exiled Nvidia leader is back in charge despite reports linking him to undisclosed romantic relationships and a separate affair. According to those reports, he carried out an affair with an alleged spy and failed to disclose his relationship with at least two subordinates.

Among the individuals named in these reports is Kimberly Powell, head of Nvidia's healthcare division. The details surrounding Huang's return remain reported speech rather than confirmed facts.
items.title: Jensen Huang Returns to Nvidia Despite Reports of Undisclosed Relationships

items.summary:
US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that he had seen enough information to conclude that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is not a security threat, while praising his administration's behind-the-scenes effort to reinstate the executive. Speaking at Mar-a-Lago, Trump told reporters 'I think he's absolutely fine,' and described saving Huang's job as 'a great thing' for both the country and the world.

When asked how he could be certain given that the Justice Department had not confirmed a thorough investigation into Huang, Trump said his judgment rested on 'information I have, which is a lot of information.' The Justice Department did not confirm having conducted such an inquiry. Huang was forced to resign earlier this month after reports that he had an affair with a business executive tied to Chinese intelligence and whose company may have helped China obtain advanced chips in violation of US export controls.

Trump said his administration worked behind the scenes to push for Huang's reinstatement, which he called 'a highly unusual intervention by the government into a top company's decision making.' He added that seeing what was happening with the company and its stock price led him to believe returning Huang would be beneficial. Nvidia's shares had fallen sharply after his resignation before partially rebounding following the board's shock decision to reinstate him.

Trump said he had not spoken with Huang since the reinstatement was announced, but later claimed that when they did speak, 'he is so happy to be going back,' calling it his 'second term.' He also praised Huang's wife as 'phenomenal.'
items.title: Trump Says Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Is Not a Security Threat

items.summary:
President Trump defended his role in bringing Jensen Huang back to lead Nvidia, calling the reinstatement a positive development for both the country and the world. Speaking at Mar-a-Lago on Thursday, Trump said he saw what was happening with the company and its stock and believed returning Huang would be 'a great thing.'

Trump described Huang's return as his 'second term' and expressed confidence that the CEO would perform even better than before. He said he had not spoken to Huang since Nvidia announced the reinstatement but expected contact before Huang resumed his role, according to Bloomberg.

When asked about national security concerns tied to Huang's personal associations, Trump dismissed them, saying 'Based on information and belief, I think he's absolutely fine.' When pressed for specifics behind that assessment, he replied: 'The information I have, which is a lot of information,' per Bloomberg. He added that he believed his decision had done 'a great thing for our country and even for the world.'

Huang's reinstatement has drawn criticism from both Republicans and Democrats over government intervention and potential counterintelligence risks. A CBS News report said US intelligence officials briefed congressional staffers that China's Ministry of State Security may have monitored Alice Huang, a woman previously associated with Jensen Huang who began an affair with him.

According to the same report, intelligence agencies had not established the full extent of any contact and found no evidence that Alice Huang was directed by China to collect information about Jensen Huang or shared data of substantial intelligence value. The concerns were reportedly summarized in a classified memorandum prepared by Secretary of State and National Security Adviser Marco Rubio for senior administration officials.

Huang is scheduled to meet House lawmakers privately on December 1, with public testimony before the Senate Banking Committee expected on December 3, per Bloomberg.
items.title: Trump Defends Jensen Huang's Return as Nvidia CEO Amid National Security Questions

items.summary:
Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong said on Friday that Singapore has not confirmed reports claiming Nvidia halted chip shipments to the country.

Gan's comments came in response to a Thursday report alleging that Nvidia had suspended chip shipments across Southeast Asia.
items.title: Singapore Unconfirmed Reports of Nvidia Chip Shipment Halt

items.summary:
Google terminated more than 19,000 Indonesian-linked YouTube channels between July and September as part of an investigation into coordinated influence operations that shared content supportive of the Indonesian government. The removal is one of the largest mass account terminations in years on the platform.

The purge ranks as the third-highest quarterly removal since 2023, behind two earlier instances involving accounts linked to Chinese influence operations. In August alone, about 10,000 channels were removed.

Indonesia's Ministry of Communication and Digital summoned Google Indonesia and YouTube Southeast Asia representatives after concluding the security bulletin did not provide sufficient supporting explanations. The ministry asked for written details on the methodology used to detect and terminate the accounts so its findings are not misinterpreted.

The dispute comes amid criticism that Komdigi itself has requested platforms remove content critical of the government, prompting civil society groups to question whether the tech giant is being held to standards it does not apply consistently. Remotivi and SAFENet found 94 posts had been removed following ministry requests.

Komdigi acknowledged errors in its own moderation actions are possible and said it would match incident records against notifications received so any mistakes can be corrected. Google's Indonesian YouTube Purge Sparks Dispute Over Transparency

Google terminated more than 19,000 Indonesian-linked YouTube channels between July and September as part of an investigation into coordinated influence operations that shared content supportive of the Indonesian government. The removal is one of the largest mass account terminations in years on the platform.

The purge ranks as the third-highest quarterly removal since 2023, behind two earlier instances involving accounts linked to Chinese influence operations. In August alone, about 10,000 channels were removed.

Indonesia's Ministry of Communication and Digital summoned Google Indonesia and YouTube Southeast Asia representatives after concluding the security bulletin did not provide sufficient supporting explanations. The ministry asked for written details on the methodology used to detect and terminate the accounts so its findings are not misinterpreted.

The dispute comes amid criticism that Komdigi itself has requested platforms remove content critical of the government, prompting civil society groups to question whether the tech giant is being held to standards it does not apply consistently. Remotivi and SAFENet found 94 posts had been removed following ministry requests.

Komdigi acknowledged errors in its own moderation actions are possible and said it would match incident records against notifications received so any mistakes can be corrected. The ministry also pressed Google and YouTube to use their detection capabilities against networks promoting online gambling or distributing pornographic content.

The US Federal Communications Commission approved SpaceX's plan to launch one million 'Starmind' artificial intelligence data centre satellites, which would multiply the number of operational satellites by a factor of 50.

SpaceX says the constellation would move AI computing into space using solar-powered satellites and beam results back to Earth. The article frames this as combining an existing satellite boom with an AI investment bubble under a Trump administration that has loosened environmental regulation.

The current operational satellite count is creeping toward 20,000, while orbital launches have risen to almost one per day; Starlink remains the best-known example of such constellations. Starmind would be far larger than any existing constellation.

Getting a million satellites into orbit would require roughly 500 satellites launched every day if they had five-year lifetimes similar to Starlink, which also implies about 500 satellites needing disposal each day through reentry and burning up in the atmosphere for those below 2,000 kilometres altitude.

When satellites burn up, their materials deposit into the upper atmosphere at quantities exceeding natural meteor inputs. Aluminium is of particular concern because alumina could destroy ozone, potentially increasing ultraviolet light on Earth and skin cancer risk; each satellite would be about 75 metres wide and brighter than any star in the early evening.

The article warns that orbital clutter raises collision risks through debris clouds and a possible Kessler Syndrome cascade. SpaceX mitigates collisions by manoeuvring satellites, but failed uncontrolled satellites remain dangerous because such manoeuvres require operational satellites to perform them.

Under the Trump administration the FCC is taking a looser regulatory approach, declining environmental review under the National Environmental Policy Act for Starmind and making statements the article calls sci-fi silliness, including claims about advancing humanity toward a Kardashev II civilization. The article rejects that claim as unfounded.
items.title: FCC approves SpaceX's plan for one million Starmind AI satellites

President Donald Trump said he had seen enough information to conclude that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is not a national security threat and described his administration's effort to reinstate Huang as 'a great thing' for the world. Huang returned to lead the AI chipmaker less than two weeks after resigning amid revelations about extra-marital affairs, including one involving a business executive allegedly linked to Chinese intelligence.

Huang's reinstatement lifted Nvidia's shares but drew criticism from lawmakers who have pledged to examine both his conduct and the Trump administration's role in bringing him back. The situation has placed Huang's future, US national security concerns, and presidential intervention at the center of a political and corporate dispute.
items.title: Trump backs Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia chief

Indian equity benchmarks recovered from early losses to post modest gains in a volatile session, with eased crude oil prices and foreign institutional investor inflows offsetting concerns over US tariff threats.

The BSE Sensex rose 390.31 points, or 0.46 per cent, to close at 84,328.59.

The NSE Nifty 50 advanced 65.25 points, or 0.25 per cent, to finish the day at 25,884.50.

Tata Consultancy Services Ltd, Prestige Estates Projects Ltd and Multi Commodity Exchange of India Ltd are among the stocks expected to attract trader attention.

Vishnu Kant Upadhyay, AVP of Research at Master Capital Services, provided commentary on these names ahead of Thursday's trading session.
items.title: Indian benchmark indices posted modest gains as eased crude and FII inflows outweighed US tariff threats

Kazushige Kamiyama, an executive director at the Bank of Japan, called on global policymakers to strengthen defences against financial stability and cybersecurity risks from new forms of digital money and infrastructure. Speaking Nov. 27 at a seminar hosted by the International Monetary Fund in Tokyo, he said these emerging technologies pose fresh challenges for regulators.

Kamiyama warned that stablecoins and tokenised deposits are likely to coexist and interact, raising concerns about fragmentation and threats to financial stability. He noted that policymakers must ensure this diversity does not undermine the system as they move beyond experiments toward establishing rules and infrastructure for wider use.

The executive director said growing AI adoption brings new cybersecurity risks because of its increasing ability to discover and exploit vulnerabilities. He stressed that authorities and institutions need stronger defences against these capabilities, which he described as requiring platforms designed with security and resilience from the outset.

items.summary:
Asian stocks were poised to close November with smaller losses after AI-related jitters eased during the holiday lull, while the US dollar was heading toward its third consecutive monthly gain.

Oil prices staged their first weekly rise in four weeks as supply-disruption concerns returned. Brent crude slipped 0.4% on Nov 27 to reach US$96.14 a barrel but remained up 3.9% for the week, after falling 18% over November.

In Asia, S&P 500 futures were up 0.8% and Nasdaq futures rose 1% as Wall Street stayed shut for Thanksgiving. Japan's Nikkei gained 0.7% to lift its weekly total to 2.7%, partially offsetting an 8.4% loss over November.

Tokyo core inflation reached a 16-month high in November, strengthening the case for a Bank of Japan rate hike as early as December. The MSCI Asia-Pacific index outside Japan rose 0.5% for the week to end up 1.9%, though it remained down 8.2% over the month.

South Korean shares rallied 2%, while China's blue chips slipped 0.2% after hitting their lowest level since June 2025 on Nov 26.

Analyst Kyle Rodda of Capital.com said November was essentially in the books and that a seasonal 'Santa Rally' currently looked unlikely, warning that uncertainty about AI growth and US rate peaks could keep volatility elevated.

The chipmaker Nvidia remained a concern after S&P placed its credit rating on watch for a possible downgrade. The company reportedly told manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers containing its chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, according to the Financial Times.

Elon Musk said every child in the US would receive two shares in his SpaceX company, pledging a gift worth about US$18 billion (S$23.2 billion).

The US dollar was set for its third monthly gain on Nov 27, rising 1.8% against major peers to reach an index level of 103.8. It benefited from expectations that the Federal Reserve would almost certainly raise rates in December and from safe-haven flows following equity selloffs.

Futures implied a 99% chance the Fed would lift rates by 25 basis points in December, while bets on a half-point increase had faded. The euro ended flat at US$1.0964 after news that Pablo Hernández de Cos was to become the next European Central Bank president, and the New Zealand dollar edged up 0.2% to US$0.5482 following an election-related political development.

Schroders chief economist David Rees said the Fed could still ease policy, but a rate cut would not necessarily be clearly positive for markets, since firm growth and inflation data might soon bring back expectations of a more hawkish central bank stance.
items.title: Asian shares end a bruising month on steadier footing; US dollar set for third monthly gain

Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut praised Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Thursday, calling him the top face of Hindutva and expressing confidence that he would continue leading the state after assembly elections.

Raut said it is commendable that Yogi has declared himself as CM's face, describing him as a capable man whom his party will win a majority in Uttar Pradesh to support. He stated that if there were no Yogi, there would be no UP.

His remarks come amid growing political activity ahead of the 2027 assembly elections and highlight uncertainty about who BJP's chief ministerial candidate will be for the next polls.

Uttar Pradesh deputy chief minister Keshav Prasad Maurya said on Wednesday that the BJP's CM candidate would be decided by its elected MLAs after the Assembly elections, indicating the party had not yet settled on a face. He told reporters that no individual decides this and that whatever happens will become clear in 2027.

Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge targeted the BJP over its performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, crediting voters with forcing Prime Minister Narendra Modi to abandon his '400 paar' slogan. He said the party fell short of its target despite Modi repeatedly invoking it during the campaign.

The BJP-led National Democratic Alliance won 36 of Uttar Pradesh's 80 Lok Sabha seats in the 2024 general elections, according to Kharge and reported figures.
items.title: Sanjay Raut backs Yogi Adityanath as UP's CM face, spotlighting BJP leadership uncertainty

The eighth NSA-level meeting of the Colombo Security Conclave in the Maldives reaffirmed member states' collective commitment to promote regional peace and security through sustained cooperation. The leaders called for strengthening collaboration across the conclave's five pillars, emphasizing training, sharing best practices, and capacity-building initiatives.

The five areas of CSC cooperation are maritime safety and security, countering terrorism and radicalisation, combating trafficking and transnational organised crime, cyber security and protection of critical infrastructure and technology, and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief. Member states including the Maldives, India, Mauritius, and Sri Lanka adopted a Roadmap of Cooperation for 2026-27 that sets out key deliverables and planned activities under these pillars.

The Colombo Security Conclave was established to promote closer cooperation on security matters and strengthen partnerships for enhancing regional security in the Indian Ocean Region. Bangladesh also participated in the meeting, though its membership remains pending as Dhaka completes internal processes required by membership requirements.

NSA Ajit Doval said India is committed to working closely with CSC nations to enhance collective capacities for addressing evolving serious security challenges.
items.title: Colombo Security Conclave Adopts 2026-27 Roadmap and Reaffirms Regional Cooperation

A CareEdge Advisory report projects India's semiconductor market will grow from about $45-50 billion in CY26E to roughly $100-110 billion by CY30P, driven by rising demand across electronics, telecommunications, automotive systems, AI, data centres and digital infrastructure.

The demand mix is shifting toward connectivity and computing. Networking and communications share should rise from 26.1% in CY20 to 33.3% by CY30 at a CAGR of 17.8%, while computing and data storage rises from 12.8% to 15.1% at a CAGR of 11.9%. Consumer electronics share is expected to fall from 29.1% to 22.2% over the same period.

Despite rising consumption, India still relies heavily on imports. Semiconductor imports more than tripled from $11.9 billion in FY21 to $36.5 billion in FY26, and DSCI estimates cited by CareEdge say imports cover 90-95% of domestic demand for semiconductor devices and components.

Under the India Semiconductor Mission, 12 projects with cumulative investments exceeding Rs 1.64 lakh crore have been approved across Gujarat, Assam, Uttar Pradesh, Odisha, Punjab and Andhra Pradesh. Five of these had begun commercial production by October 2026, according to a government update.

Tanvi Shah of CareEdge said the bigger opportunity lies in converting India's chip-design strength and approved investments into commercially viable fabrication, testing and advanced-packaging capabilities, with timely execution, technology access, skilled talent and supplier ecosystem development as key enablers. Praveen Pardeshi added that the next phase will focus on turning announced projects into measurable outcomes such as operating capacity, local value addition and supply chain integration.
items.title: India's semiconductor market projected to reach $100-110 billion by 2030

The final New Zealand general election results show the National-led rightwing coalition needs a deal with the newcomer centrist Opportunity party to form a government and avoid another poll. Preliminary returns had given National, New Zealand First and Act only a two-seat majority, but after nearly 485,000 special votes were tallied on Friday, the bloc fell one seat short of power.

The National-led coalition now holds 65 seats in the 130-seat parliament, which requires 66 for a majority. National dropped two seats to finish with 40; Labour held 36 and grew from three to four seats as the Greens picked up one seat to reach 17.

Opportunity has said it will negotiate first with whichever party wins the most seats, so its talks are expected to begin with Luxon's National. Opportunity leader Qiulae Wong confirmed she would speak with Luxon and that her bottom lines on climate policy and capping political donations were non-negotiable, while stressing a priority for government stability.

The deal could be complicated by New Zealand First refusing to work with Opportunity if Winston Peters serves as foreign affairs minister. Other tensions include the opposing climate policies of New Zealand First and Act, plus Act's likely opposition to donation reforms.

National still faces an outside chance at power without Opportunity: a recount application due 3 December could return it to government if it wins back just one electorate seat lost in special votes.
items.title: New Zealand election results leave ruling coalition dependent on centrist Opportunity party

The Japanese health ministry is weighing a premium increase on nursing care insurance for older people earning ¥1.2 million ($7,500) or more annually after public pension and other deductions, with the change set to take effect in fiscal 2027.

Sources reported Thursday that the plan targets higher-income seniors as part of broader reforms to a system strained by Japan's aging population and rising demand for nursing care services. The ministry also intends measures to ease premium costs on low-income earners, per review plans presented at a Social Security Council meeting.

The nursing care insurance system collects premiums from people aged 65 and older, with municipal governments setting standard amounts that are reviewed every three years. The nationwide average for the period between fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2026 is ¥6,225 per month.
items.title: Japan health ministry considering higher nursing care premiums for some older adults

A JPMorgan report estimates that artificial intelligence displacement could affect about 1.3 per cent of the global knowledge workforce annually over five years.

The estimate relies on a scenario in which half of potential enterprise AI spending goes toward replacing jobs, with AI costing roughly half as much as the workers it replaces.

JPMorgan says much of this adjustment could come through unfilled roles rather than layoffs, but warns that concentration in particular occupations or regions could create greater economic and political pressure.

If two-thirds of displaced roles were located in the United States, around 16 million workers could be affected over five years, or roughly 3 million annually.

The report notes AI adoption is still early: only 6 per cent of work hours in the United States are currently AI-assisted, even though about two-thirds of tasks may theoretically be exposed to it.

JPMorgan argues that wider adoption beyond the technology sector would be needed for AI investments to deliver expected returns, with businesses moving past pilot programmes and using the technology more extensively.
items.title: JPMorgan report warns AI could displace millions of jobs globally

Japan's reported five-year defence budget falls short of the military spending that some officials and lawmakers had assumed, according to Reuters. The figure sits within a 50 trillion yen to 60 trillion yen range proposed by Finance Ministry officials for the period starting in April 2027.

The allocation exceeds the current four-year plan's 43 trillion yen but remains well below the 80 trillion yen budget that some defence officials and ruling Liberal Democratic Party lawmakers had assumed during negotiations with contractors. Reuters attributes these figures to its own calculations and reporting.

Under this budget, Japan would miss its target of raising defence spending to 2% of gross domestic product, according to Reuters calculations. The government plans to revise its national security strategy and related defence documents by year-end.
items.title: Japan's Defence Budget Falls Short of Military Demand

A growing trend sees people increasingly book tables for one as a form of self-care and independence rather than because they are away from friends or family. Catherine Smith, 23, from Yorkshire, dines alone at least once a month at high-end restaurants she would not usually visit with others.

Food trends analyst Charles Banks describes eating alone as 'an intentional act' that has become almost aspirational amid social changes. But he warns the trend is not universally welcomed: some diners may feel like an inefficient use of a table rather than a customer a restaurant wants.

OpenTable, which covers more than 5,000 restaurants in the UK, says solo dining makes up its smallest proportion of bookings but is the fastest-growing category. Bookings from January to August this year rose by 23% compared with the same period last year, though OpenTable did not provide data for verification.

SoloTable found that one in eight of 178 restaurants surveyed in London does not accept online reservations from solo diners. Some venues are adapting instead: Jungli, an Indian restaurant in Newcastle upon Tyne, has added high tables and bar seats plus charging points to make solo dining more comfortable.
items.title: Solo dining is the fastest-growing restaurant booking category in the UK

A catastrophic Aug. 26 flood killed more than 1,353 people and reopened the debate over building large reservoir dams in Nepal's Himalayas.

Proponents argue high dams could absorb floods, ease winter power shortages, and protect water supplies as glaciers shrink; opponents warn stored water adds risk if a glacial lake bursts and favor solar or pumped storage instead.

Research shows Himalayan hydropower is broadly exposed to such floods, but no study has yet tested whether reservoirs actually worsen them. Engineers also say dams may not be able to check the size of debris-laden flood like August's.

Diplomatic efforts remain stalled as Iran told Washington it would not restore Strait of Hormuz shipping until its demands are met, including lifting the US naval blockade and ending hostilities across all fronts; Tehran offered to reopen the waterway within 48 hours through Qatari mediation if those conditions were accepted.

Goldman Sachs raised its December Brent forecast to $105 a barrel from $90 earlier this month and lifted its WTI projection to $94 from $81, warning that sustained Gulf supply shortfalls could push Brent toward $140 in 2027 under a bullish scenario averaging around $130.

The bank's projections factor in geopolitical uncertainty adding a risk premium through potential Middle East supply disruptions and the difficulty of reaching a lasting diplomatic settlement. JPMorgan similarly flagged conflict-related uncertainty, noting that several economic thresholds it had expected to be avoided have already been crossed after seven months without a clear path to ending the war.

Despite these longer-term risks, near-term expectations of increased exports continue to press on prices.

Speaking at the International Monetary Fund's seminar on digital money and payments in Tokyo, he said technological innovation offers significant opportunities to improve money and payments but must be paired with trust.

Kamiyama noted that emerging digital assets such as stablecoins and tokenised deposits are likely to co-exist and interact, creating challenges for policymakers who must ensure this diversity does not cause unnecessary fragmentation or undermine financial stability. He added that the growing use of AI brings fresh cybersecurity risks because it increases the ability of bad actors to discover and exploit vulnerabilities.

The executive director emphasized that central bank money will continue to serve as the anchor of trust in the monetary system, even as tokenisation—the process of converting assets like bonds, deposits, and securities into digital tokens for trading on programmable platforms—grows. He said policymakers worldwide are moving beyond experiments toward establishing rules and infrastructure while keeping tokenised finance within regulated money and the traditional financial system.

Kamiyama cautioned that tokenisation may amplify market movements during times of stress by creating new channels of trading across institutions and markets, and that interconnected platforms could allow cyber incidents to spread quickly. He said these risks require vigilance and that new platforms must be designed with security and resilience from the outset.

Australia's largest exporters will be required to reserve up to 20 percent of their gas for domestic use, a scheme that passed parliament with the Coalition supporting Labor after weeks of negotiation.

The legislation was waved through in a late-night Senate sitting on Thursday and rubber-stamped by the lower house shortly afterward. Resources Minister Madeleine King said it would deliver cheaper gas prices but declined to name an exact figure, warning that naming one could become a price floor.

Resources Minister Madeleine King noted Western Australia's existing scheme since 2008 inspired the national plan, granting WA a permanent carve-out after lobbying from the Coalition and Premier Roger Cook. Under that state scheme, exporters must reserve 15 percent of LNG for domestic use over a development's life; delivery to the domestic market was 8.7 percent in 2021 and rose to 12.5 percent by 2025.

The key sticking point between Labor and the Coalition was a requirement that gas companies oversupply the market by 10 percent, designed to lower prices for households and industry; it will remain in place after the Coalition secured a statutory review of its investment impact after five years.

Industry Minister Tim Ayres said Australia would stay a reliable supplier and described the plan as proportional domestic contribution rather than an export ban or cap. The Greens voted against the scheme in its current form, having demanded a 25 percent tax on gas exports instead.

At recent peace talks in Abu Dhabi between Russia, the United States, and Ukraine, Russian negotiators pushed for a new European security architecture that Washington has signaled openness to. In a speech at a Minsk conference this month, Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov outlined what such a framework might entail: an arrangement spanning all of Europe and Asia built on 'sovereignty,' 'equality,' and 'indivisible security.'

Lavrov framed the proposal partly as a response to NATO's expansion eastward despite past assurances against it. He also claimed the West is now forming a new 'NATO-style military-political bloc in Asia' that Russia opposes. While he said Europe was welcome to join, Lavrov added that Russia remains ready for war if European states initiate one.

The article argues several factors make broad acceptance of this framework unlikely. The prevailing view across Europe treats Russia as the continent's principal security threat, making it improbable that European states would agree to a Russian-led arrangement. Moscow has also made clear it does not want European representatives in Ukraine peace talks, which suggests Europe may have no voice in any future agreement.

European attitudes toward Russia are shifting amid mounting economic pressures and rising support for right-wing parties. The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) opposes funding or arming Ukraine on national-interest grounds and has called for closer energy ties with Russia and the revival of Russian language teaching, according to its platform in a recent eastern state election.

Some Europeans have floated alternatives such as strengthening the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe or reviving the NATO-Russia Council. The article notes these options seem far-fetched given the absence of trust between Moscow and Kyiv. Many observers believe Russia's true aim is to divide the continent into Cold War-style spheres of influence.

The proposal also faces uncertainty over how China fits into it, since Beijing pursues its own security ambitions and has long emphasized non-interference in other states' affairs. China promotes initiatives like the Belt and Road Initiative and often advances its own vision of international order. The two powers cooperate closely but compete for influence in Central Asia.

Eurasia already contains numerous overlapping organizations with distinct interests, including the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, BRICS, and the Gulf Cooperation Council. It is unclear how a Russia-led framework would interact with or compete against these groups. There appears to be growing preference in Asia for smaller ideological alliances—such as the pact between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey—and non-aligned nations like those in Southeast Asia favor partnerships that serve varied interests.

The article concludes that while Russia's aims echo Soviet-era influence, new international orders do not emerge overnight but evolve through states pursuing their own interests. It suggests too many hurdles stand between Moscow's vision and its realization as the post–World War II order gradually erodes.
items.title: Russia's Proposed Eurasian Security Framework Faces Multiple Hurdles

Nathan Lyon is expected to be dropped from the Australian squad for the upcoming Test series against New Zealand.

Lyon, 39, has taken 577 wickets across 145 Tests for Australia in his career.

The four-match series begins with its opening Test at Perth on December 9.
items.title: Nathan Lyon set to miss New Zealand Test series amid career uncertainty

items.summary:
A powerful Nor'easter storm disrupted Thanksgiving celebrations across the United States, knocking out power to nearly a million homes and cancelling hundreds of flights as families prepared for holiday gatherings.

According to PowerOutage.us data cited by Reuters, more than 961,000 US utility customers were without electricity at 7:30 pm ET. Pennsylvania was the worst-hit state with over 235,000 outages, followed by New Jersey (180,000), Maryland (156,000), Virginia (132,000), Missouri (106,000), New York (56,000) and Delaware (21,000).

The storm forced roughly 400 flights to be cancelled and more than 2,000 delayed across the country according to FlightAware data. Most of these disruptions occurred in the eastern United States.

Heavy rain and strong winds from the Nor'easter prompted authorities to close major bridges due to high winds and caused trees to fall onto power lines and homes as waterlogged ground weakened them.

The Macy's 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade was postponed for Saturday, marking the first time in its history that the annual event has been delayed. New York and New Jersey governors declared states of emergency over damaging winds, heavy rainfall and severe coastal flooding expected through Friday.

Citing AccuWeather meteorologist Alyssa Glenny via Bloomberg, wind gusts had reached 72 miles per hour at Stingray Point in Virginia while coastal areas of New Jersey and Long Island braced for gusts up to 80 mph as the storm moved northward. The National Weather Service issued coastal flood warnings covering all five boroughs of New York City.

In Maryland's suburbs near Washington, authorities urged nearly two million customers to limit tap water consumption because power cuts could disrupt the water treatment system.
items.title: Nor'easter Storm Disrupts Thanksgiving Across the US East Coast

The US dollar index closed Friday near a 22-month high at 103.81, steady after spiking to 104.53 on Monday and then losing those gains the next day.

Trading was thin because of holiday schedules, and investors were watching equity markets for direction as concerns about the AI trade increased volatility in currency markets.

The dollar strengthened slightly during Friday's Asian session against both the yen at 159.355 and the Swiss franc at 0.83455, while the euro held around $1.0964 and sterling eased to $1.3099.

Mizuho analysts said whether AI-related stocks reverse their decline would be decisive for risk-sensitive currencies such as the Australian dollar and Mexican peso, which could bounce back on a recovery or face renewed selling pressure if weakness continued.

The currency's strength is supported by expectations of Federal Reserve rate hikes, with traders viewing a quarter-point increase on December 9 as nearly certain according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.
items.title: Dollar Holds Near 22-Month Peak as AI Trade Doubts Weigh on Risk Currencies

The UK will pay an additional 'participation fee' of 4% on top of its main contribution to the running costs of three EU agencies and systems needed to deliver two agreements agreed by Prime Minister Andy Burnham, according to legal documents. The surcharge applies in addition to a base operational contribution calculated as a share of the UK economy's size relative to that of the EU, broadly mirroring how member states split their contributions to the bloc's budget.

The government has said it expects total additional costs from the deals to be in the low tens of millions per year and 'massively outweighed' by predicted economic gains. Officials have not yet published an estimate of overall extra costs. The two agreements, on aligning with EU food standards and re-linking Britain to its carbon trading regime, are meant to take effect during 2028.

Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said the deals were 'not about cost to the taxpayer'. Ministers declined to give specifics of the fees during negotiations. Legal text for a third agreement on youth visas for people aged 18 to 31 is expected to be published in the coming days.

The government also published separate legislation granting it broad powers to incorporate new EU laws required to implement the agreements without holding a full vote each time, which has drawn criticism from opposition parties. Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said Burnham was showing 'disdain for the democratic process' by seeking what she called a blank cheque while having no idea what the EU would agree to.

Reform UK leader Nigel Farage argued that the deals would take Britain back into much of the European Union's single market and dismissed claims that closer ties with the EU would boost growth. The government says it will have input on new rules through observer status in certain meetings, even though the UK no longer has voting rights at the EU.
items.title: UK To Pay Participation Fee As Part Of Deals With EU

The son of two elderly victims recovered his father's wristwatch from the wreckage after they were killed in last year's Hong Kong tower-block blaze.

Mr So, who uses only his surname, said his parents' watches both stopped at the moment each died. He found one watch among the ashes and brought it to show on camera.

His parents, both in their 80s, were among the 168 people killed when the first building of the Wang Fuk Court complex caught fire - the deadliest such disaster Hong Kong had seen in decades.

Their bodies were burned beyond recognition. Mr So visited his parents' grave and filmed what remained of their possessions after the blaze.
items.title: Son finds father's stopped watch in ashes of Hong Kong tower fire

The US has proposed a 25% tariff on Indian imports, with the rate falling to 17% if a long-pending trade deal is reached. Unlike other nations in scope of broad tariffs, India alone has not yet signed an agreement despite beginning talks in February 2025.

At 17%, the contingent rate for India would be lower than rates planned for several key competitors, potentially giving Indian exporters a competitive edge. The Trump administration proposes 18% for Bangladesh, Cambodia and Indonesia, and 20% for Vietnam if it strikes a trade deal.

China faces a current 20% rate under an expiring US-China truce that lapses on January 10, rising to 40% if the truce collapses. China's 20% would also be added to roughly 25% in duties imposed during Trump's first term.

The potential 17% for India is below the 18% agreed under a February framework deal that predated the Supreme Court striking down emergency tariff powers, which now sets a global baseline of 10%.

The US accuses India of inadequate labour protections, financial repression, market access barriers and failure to address excess capacity. New Delhi's trade ministry said it was examining the notice from the US Trade Representative and stated during its investigation that India has no structural excess capacity in any sector.
items.title: Trump's Proposed India Tariffs Compared With Rival Nations

Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar, a rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP, said the delimitation Bill would make lawmakers' work easier while adding that her group will decide its stance after reviewing the bill.

The 20 TMC rebels whose proposed merger with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India is awaiting approval from the Lok Sabha Speaker could influence whether the delimitation Bill passes during Parliament's four-day special sitting.

In an interview with Hindustan Times, Ghosh Dastidar said her group had not received a formal briefing on the agenda and would prepare to travel after seeing Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju's post about the government business.

She noted that in April the rebels discussed delimitation as a constitutional provision tied to census and population data, arguing it gives MPs clearer constituencies to approach for governance. She said they will follow the Constitution once told what bill is coming.

When asked whether voters would gain or lose political weight under the new scheme, Ghosh Dastidar declined to comment, saying her group does not yet know which bill is being tabled and will discuss it only after receiving details.
items.title: Rebel TMC MP Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar Says Delimitation Will Ease MPs' Work Ahead of House Sitting

Delhi's air remained in the 'poor' category on Thursday, with the Central Pollution Control Board reporting an AQI of 220 at 8am and a 24-hour average of 224.

Thirteen of Delhi's 57 monitoring stations recorded 'very poor' air quality, while 27 were in the 'poor' category and 17 in the 'moderate' category. These figures come from CPCB data on its website.

Delhi Technological University logged the highest AQI at 335, while Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium recorded the lowest reading at 130 among the stations reported by DTU and others.

Unfavourable weather conditions limited pollutant dispersal. An inversion layer formed around 300 metres above the ground at 4:30am on Friday with surface temperatures nearly 10°C lower, up from about 150 metres a day earlier.
items.title: Delhi air quality rated 'poor' as PM2.5 stays main pollutant

Europe's largest software company SAP SE is reportedly preparing to cut at least 10,000 positions as part of a sweeping restructuring aimed at repositioning the business for an artificial intelligence era. The report comes from Bloomberg and describes the layoffs as affecting at least 9% of the global workforce.

The final number of job cuts has not been determined, according to the report, which adds that it could change after discussions with labour representatives. SAP currently employs more than 110,000 people worldwide.

Chief executive Christian Klein accelerated the restructuring as he repositions the company around artificial intelligence. The plan involves redesigning how SAP develops and sells software products, with a strong focus on embedding AI capabilities across its application portfolio.
items.title: SAP plans to cut at least 10,000 jobs in AI-driven restructuring

items.summary:
Content creator Monsoon Dey said she earned more than Rs 10 lakh in October, making it her highest-earning month so far. She attributed the figure to festive campaigns and user-generated content rather than a fixed salary.

Dey credited timing for much of the success: about 90% of her deals were tied to Durga Puja because she understood how important the festival is to Bengali-speaking audiences, and brands buy into a creator's culture as well as their product. She said being able to work in Bengali, Hindi and English helped her connect with those campaigns.

She completed 16 brand collaborations plus one user-generated content video by shooting and delivering videos within the same day even during the festival, while also posting more than 30 pieces of organic content that month. Her individual rates were not fixed; deals ranged between Rs 60,000 and Rs 1 lakh depending on deliverables and usage rights.

Dey clarified several caveats about her earnings: the amount had not fully reached her bank account because brands typically pay within 30 to 60 days, so earned income and received cash can differ at any given time. She also stressed that freelance income fluctuates every month depending on project volume, seasonal campaigns and payment schedules.

She said she has a chartered accountant and files taxes, and concluded that social media is one of the biggest opportunities to build serious wealth when creativity combines with consistency, audience understanding and professional execution.
items.title: Bengaluru creator earned over Rs 10 lakh in October through brand deals

While Bihar strongman Anant Singh's daughter Shivangi's wedding on November 25 drew national attention, Jharkhand BJP MP Dhulu Mahto hosted an equally grand shaadi for his eldest daughter Sakshi in the neighboring coal belt of Dhanbad a day earlier. The two weddings occurred within roughly 24 hours and at comparable scale, yet only one captured headlines.

Dhulu Mahto married Sakshi Kumari to Ravikant Saw, reportedly a deputy superintendent of police from Bokaro district, on Tuesday (November 24) in his native village of Chitahi. The venue featured dozens of elaborate pandals, ornamental gateways and decorative lights that local vloggers likened to Durga Puja pandals.

Food was arranged for between 1.5 lakh and two lakh people across eight locations including the football ground, Ramraj temple premises and Khas Tundu, with separate arrangements for VIP and VVIP guests. The jaimala stage drew comparisons with a Tirupati Balaji-style setup in Andhra Pradesh, while artists from six states performed cultural tableaux.

The gathering crossed party lines: Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren visited to bless the couple alongside Union Minister Annapurna Devi, Leader of Opposition Babulal Marandi and state BJP president Aditya Sahu. Bihar Assembly Speaker Prem Kumar also attended Mahto's wedding a day before braving a 10-km traffic jam at Shivangi's.

Officials inspected security arrangements ahead of the event, including a helipad near Ramraj temple for high-profile guests and restrictions on heavy vehicles along a four-lane stretch between Rahul Chowk and Mahuda More. Despite the scale, Mahto's wedding reportedly ran smoothly compared with the chaos that followed Anant Singh's feast.

Anant Singh had prepared to feed around four lakh people at Nadwan in Patna district, serving over 150 dishes and hosting a horse race with a Mahindra Thar as the prize. Videos of crowds scrambling for food and traffic congestion dominated social media, while Mahto credited his aides and supporters—extending invitations even to those without cards—for making the elaborate arrangements possible.

Besiktas defeated Hapoel Beer-Sheva 2-1 on Thursday to win the fifth matchday of the UEFA Europa League league phase, a victory secured despite an approximately 30-minute suspension caused by clashes between Georgian police and supporters in the stands.

The disruption began in the 26th minute after reports that police intervened following a fan displaying a Palestinian flag; officers used pepper spray and surrounded the supporter. Footage later showed one Besiktas fan being carried out on a stretcher, with many others injured by the intervention.

Besiktas kept their lead intact through two late goals: Junior Olaitan scored in the 75th minute to break the deadlock after Hapoel Beer-Sheva failed to clear Kassoum Ouattara's cross, and Orkun Kokcu added a second with a powerful shot from the right side of the penalty area in the 90th minute.

Hapoel Beer-Sheva pulled one back in stoppage time when Javon East converted an assist from Joao Victor to make it 2-1, but Besiktas held on for the win. Kokcu extended his European scoring run this season with goals against Celtic, Kauno Zalgiris and FC Midtjylland.

The Turkish side had failed to score in regulation after goalkeeper Dogan Alemdar made several key saves in the first half, including stops of Muhammad Abu Rumi and Amankwah Forson. Besiktas only took the lead through a penalty awarded for handball by Miguel Vitor, which Orkun Kokcu missed before scoring late.
items.title: Besiktas beat Hapoel Beer-Sheva 2-1 in Europa League match disrupted by police intervention

A JPMorgan Wealth Management report projects that artificial intelligence could displace about 24 million knowledge-worker jobs worldwide within the next five years under an illustrative scenario in which half of enterprise AI spending replaces roles and costs roughly half as much as the workers it substitutes.

The firm frames this displacement as affecting around 1.3 per cent of the global knowledge workforce each year, noting that most of the adjustment could occur through unfilled positions rather than outright layoffs.

JPMorgan warns the risk would be greater if job losses concentrate in specific occupations or regions, potentially generating more economic and political pressure.

For the United States, the report says two-thirds of displaced roles located there would mean about 16 million workers affected over five years, roughly 3 million annually, equating to around 2 per cent of payrolls each year—more than four times manufacturing job losses in the 2000s and approaching Great Recession-era rates but sustained across a longer period.

The bank says this large-scale displacement is less likely than disruption within jobs, because AI currently automates or augments only part of every role's tasks rather than eliminating entire positions.
items.title: JPMorgan report estimates AI could displace around 24 million knowledge-worker jobs over five years

Three party leaders are competing in Spain's general election on Sunday, which leftist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez called after a parliamentary setback over housing legislation that highlighted the fragility of his minority coalition government.

Javier Carbonell, a policy analyst at the European Policy Centre speaking with FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney, said that despite solid economic growth in Spain, citizens have endured a housing crisis and inflation. He argued that people remain angry with the government and the economic system regardless of favorable macroeconomic data.

Carbonell added that this anger is directed at the establishment, identifying Sanchez as the immediate target while warning that citizens may soon turn their frustration toward the PP and Vox.
items.title: Spain Heads to Polls Amid Public Anger With Establishment

The Indian government plans to deploy a fifth S-400 air defence system along the 740 km Line of Control in Jammu and Kashmir, according to two officials cited by Hindustan Times. The deployment would add to three existing systems in Punjab, Rajasthan and Gujarat.

India already operates a fourth S-400 system in Assam to protect an 1126 km stretch of the Line of Actual Control with Arunachal Pradesh, per the same officials. An Indian Air Force pre-dispatch inspection team is scheduled to visit Russia next month, and the fifth system should be ready for deployment by February 2027.

The S-400 can counter ballistic missiles, aircraft, drones and loitering munitions from a range of 40 km to 400 km. India is seeking to buy another five systems from Russia over the coming year.

Officials said the decision follows reports that China plans to supply J-35 fifth-generation fighters to Pakistan in 2027, Washington is providing an F-16 upgrade package, and Saudi Arabia is releasing capital tied to its support against Iranian-backed Houthis. The officials attributed these claims as reported assessments rather than confirmed facts.

India reportedly intends to develop long-range stand-off weapons and loitering munitions to counter Chinese missiles such as the PL-15 E and air defence systems like the HQ 9BE, citing Pakistan's use of J-10 fighters with Swedish AWACS during Operation Sindoor. Officials also noted that Pakistan is acquiring eight Hangor-class submarines from China for over $5 billion.

Turkey reportedly is upgrading Agosta 90 B submarines and supplying kamikaze drones to Pakistan, while China has already provided armed Wing Loong II drones. The officials framed these acquisitions as the basis for India's plan to strengthen its western border infrastructure.
items.title: India to Deploy Fifth S-400 System Along Jammu & Kashmir Line of Control

Chief Minister Mohan Yadav and union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan will jointly inaugurate the Narmada Seep-Ambar Irrigation Project in Bhairunda, a village under Budhni assembly constituency in Madhya Pradesh.

The project costs ₹536 crore (ev1) and is designed to irrigate 30,000 hectares across 76 villages through water supplied via the scheme (ev2, ev3).

Construction will proceed in two phases, with an additional foundation of development and construction works worth ₹40 crore laid down where canals are replaced (ev4).

The inauguration coincides with a Diwali Milan function organized by legislator Ramakant Bhargava.

Both leaders had been apart after a rift widened following the government's removal of temporary constructions built by tribal people on forestland in Budhni. Senior BJP leaders later narrowed the divide, and Yadav met Chouhan in Delhi with several officers before attending the public function together.
items.title: MP Chief Minister and Union Minister to Inaugurate ₹536 Crore Irrigation Project

Severe storms brought flooding, strong winds, and widespread power outages across parts of the United States on Thanksgiving, disrupting holiday travel. Streets were inundated in New Jersey's Sea Isle City and Ocean City, with Avalon reporting some of its worst flooding ever; a few drivers had to be rescued after driving into floodwaters but no injuries occurred.

Macy's postponed its 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade in Manhattan until Saturday, citing caution about how the giant balloons would fare in windy conditions. The National Weather Service warned of disruption at eastern US airports through Friday morning due to poor visibility, turbulence, strong winds, and ice forming on aircraft.

More than 600,000 homes and businesses lost power Thursday afternoon, mostly in East Coast states, according to the outage tracking website poweroutage.us. Wind gusts of 80 km/h or higher were expected along Interstate 95, with all of New Jersey under a state of emergency declared by Governor Mikie Sherrill and parts of New York under one from Governor Kathy Hochul.

Rain and snow also hit Missouri, where up to 33 cm of snow was expected; heavy snow partly collapsed the roof of the Wentzville Ice Arena. On the West Coast, coastal flood warnings were issued from Southern California to Oregon and Washington because of king tides caused by aligned moon and sun gravity, and a wave tore down part of a pier in Pacifica, California.

Although both coasts faced flooding, travel is typically busier in the days leading up to Thanksgiving than on the holiday itself.

A paper by former senior Treasury officials John Kingman and Shriti Vadera argues that strong competition is essential to economic growth, but active pro-competition policy has become a blind spot in current UK government thinking.

The authors contend that about 60% of the fall in the UK's productivity rate since 2007 stems from reduced dynamism. They cite government Industrial Strategy Advisory Council figures showing firms under five years old accounted for 18% of all business sales in 2005, dropping to just 10% by 2021.

Kingman and Vadera claim ministers of both parties have grown less interested in competition as a growth source and more inclined to seek approval from incumbent businesses. They note that pro-growth interventions such as the City's big bang under Thatcher and the breakup of the BAA airport monopoly under Brown show past governments did support competition.

The paper says it has only been recently that active competition policy is viewed as a threat to growth rather than its driver, an attitude the authors say matters especially in the age of AI.
items.title: Former Treasury officials warn UK growth policy ignores competition

Former INX Media CEO Indrani Mukerjea told a court she did not meet her daughter Sheena Bora on April 24, 2012, the day prosecutors allege she was murdered. The accused also rejected claims that she used Skype to coordinate the killing.

Prosecutors allege Indrani, with former husband Sanjeev Khanna and driver Shyamvar Rai, killed Sheena on that date, then burnt her body and dumped it in Maharashtra's Raigad district. Investigators say the three attempted to kill Sheena's brother Mikhail as well but he escaped.

During court proceedings, Indrani was confronted with statements from approver Rai, who said she had instructed him to create a Skype account for his secretary Kajal Sharma so she could relay instructions about killing Sheena and Mikhail. Indrani denied ever speaking to Rai over the platform.

Rai also testified that Indrani asked him to arrange a car after he returned to India and accompanied him in searching for a location to dispose of the bodies, before allegedly contacting Peter Mukerjea. Indrani called this account false and denied making the call.

She further rejected allegations that she bought medicines prosecutors say were sedatives meant to be mixed with water and given to Sheena. The prosecution maintains these drugs would have been used against her daughter.

Former husband Sanjeev Khanna told the court he never met Sheena and had only seen Mikhail when he appeared as a witness during the trial. Peter Mukerjea said he knew nothing about the incident and was abroad at the time.

The accused denied all allegations as the trial continues.
items.title: Indrani Mukerjea Denies Meeting Daughter on Alleged Murder Date
